AHOY MARSHALL FAMILIES ⚓📚

March 23–27, 2026 we will be celebrating Right to Read Week with a fun, pirate-themed adventure: BOOKaneers - Finding Treasure in Books! 
Right to Read Week is a special time when we celebrate the joy and importance of reading in our school community. We are so excited for a fun week filled with books, creativity, and activities that help our students grow as readers! To help families plan ahead, we wanted to share the details early. Below you will find our dress-up schedule for the week, along with some simple activities you can do at home to celebrate reading with your child. We have also included a special RAH sheet for students to complete. All of these items are coming home with your child today as well.Thank you for partnering with us and helping make Right to Read Week a memorable and meaningful experience for our students!Stephanie JonesPrincipal

summary: **Right to Read Week** will be celebrated March 23-27, 2026 with a pirate-themed "BOOKaneers - Finding Treasure in Books" adventure. Each day features optional dress-up themes (students choose one of two options per day) worth 10 doubloons each: **Monday** - shirts with words OR red/black/white colors; **Tuesday** - fun hats OR sparkly hair accessories; **Wednesday** - bright bold colors OR wacky mismatched clothes; **Thursday** - Peter Pan characters OR Captain Hook/pirates; **Friday** - gold/silver/shiny colors OR jewel-tone colors. Students can also complete "Reading Isles" activities (Mermaid Lagoon, Shipwreck Island, Plankwalk Bay, Skull Island, and Treasure Island) earning 10 doubloons each. Materials are being sent home today.

AHOY  

MARSHALL  

FAMILIES 

⚓📚

AHOY  MARSHALL  FAMILIES ⚓📚

March 23–27, 2026 we will be celebrating Right to Read Week with a fun, pirate-themed adventure: BOOKaneers - Finding Treasure in Books! 
Right to Read Week is a special time when we celebrate the joy and importance of reading in our school community. We are so excited for a fun week filled with books, creativity, and activities that help our students grow as readers! To help families plan ahead, we wanted to share the details early. Below you will find our dress-up schedule for the week, along with some simple activities you can do at home to celebrate reading with your child. We have also included a special RAH sheet for students to complete. All of these items are coming home with your child today as well. As part of our celebration, students will have the opportunity to invite a VIP (Very Important Pirate) to join them during their scheduled library time. VIPs may be parents, grandparents, special family members, or other important adults in your child’s life.During this special visit, VIPs and students will:Read together (bring a favorite book from home or choose one from our library collection)Complete a fun directed drawing activityPlay a gameWe kindly ask all VIPs to sign up using this link so we can plan accordingly. (If you have more than one student, please fill one out for each student.) Additionally, any grown-up who would like to attend must have a completed volunteer application on file prior to coming in. The form can be emailed directly to Mrs. Jones or returned to your child’s teacher. If you have already completed a volunteer application and have one on file with the school, you are all set—no need to complete another one.On the day of your visit, please arrive 5–10 minutes before your child’s scheduled library time. VIP’s will need to bring an ID and sign in at the office. A staff member will greet VIPs and walk the group up to the library when it is time for the class to begin.Thank you for partnering with us and helping make Right to Read Week a memorable and meaningful experience for our students!

We look forward to welcoming our VIPs aboard for this exciting week of literacy fun!If you have any questions, please feel free to contact Mrs. Jones @ joness@talawanda.org or 513-273-3600.Stephanie JonesPrincipal

summary:
Marshall Elementary has released its **breakfast and lunch menus for March 2026**. 

**Breakfast highlights** include chocolate donuts, breakfast pizza, egg & cheese sandwiches, mini pancakes, glazed donuts, biscuits & gravy, French toast varieties, and themed items for St. Patrick's Day and spring. All breakfasts include 100% fruit juice, apples, oranges or other fresh fruit, and choice of milk.

**Lunch highlights** feature cheeseburgers, walking tacos, BBQ chicken, pizza options, chicken nuggets, spaghetti, hot dogs, chicken patties, mozzarella sticks, and special St. Patrick's Day and spring-themed meals. Choice of milk is included with every lunch.

Spring break begins March 30-31, 2026.

TITLE TALK - READING CORNER
Here is a post from Literacy Now with 10 ideas to do with your family while reading aloud to them. Please reach out to your student’s Reading Corner teacher with any questions.

summary: Reading activities during Spring Break help maintain student literacy skills while making reading feel like play, not schoolwork. Suggested activities include: reading a book then watching its movie adaptation (like Charlotte's Web or Curious George), reading about places visited during travel (zoos, museums, natural areas), and doing family read-alouds where everyone takes turns reading and discussing the book over meals or campfires. Contact your student's Reading Corner teacher with questions.
